findings.text: blocking: the nearest-match candidate list is sorted(_PLAN_SET_TOP) + sorted(_PLAN_SET_KEYED_FORMS), which treats the keyed heads as settable on their own, so the refusal closes with "nearest settable path 'gates'" for an input of gate and "nearest settable path 'sections'" for section (probed on the built module at head 171cb2b77) while the writer accepts neither as a bare path (gates.ID.FIELD at reckon/_store.py:2779, sections.<id>.<field> at reckon/_store.py:2708); a caller who follows the suggestion is refused again, which is the failure this node exists to remove.

follow-on: _PLAN_SET_KEYED_FORMS omits the followups.ID.FIELD form the writer handles at reckon/_store.py:2774, so the message's 'keyed forms:' clause is not the set of keyed forms, and because the nearest-match candidates come from the same table a misspelled followups path gets no nearest match at all (the message for 'followup' ends at the keyed-forms clause).

follow-on: difflib is imported inside _nearest_settable_path while reckon/_store.py imports its other stdlib names at module scope (reckon/_store.py:68); the file's function-local imports exist for reckon-internal cycles, which a stdlib import does not risk.
